chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who entrusted a man with a thousand dirhams, so it was lost. So the man said, 'It was an entrustment (wadi'ah) with me,' and the other one said, 'It was merely a loan (qard) upon you.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The wealth remains obligated for him (the borrower) unless he establishes the proof that it was an entrustment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the default legal ruling when a deposit is disputed as either a trust or a loan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-asl al-baqa' (the default is retention) in financial disputes, ruling that the money remains with the holder unless the depositor provides evidence it was a trust (wadi'ah). In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction is critical because a loan (qard) requires repayment of the principal regardless of loss, whereas a trust exempts the holder from repayment if the item is lost without negligence. The ruling underscores the evidentiary burden placed on the claimant to overturn the presumption of ownership held by the possessor.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hamma Bin Usman, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a man who entrusted a man with a thousand Dirhams, so it was wasted. So the man said, ‘It is an entrustment with me’, and the other one said, ‘But rather it was a loan upon you’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The wealth would be obligated for him (to repay) except if he establishes the proof that it was an entrustment’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who borrowed one thousand dirham and it was lost and he said that it was Wadi ‘ah (safe deposit) with him and the other said that it was a debt on him. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is responsible for it unless he presents proof that it was Wadi ‘ah (safe deposit).”’
